title: Materials Science
description: An explicitly partial foundational university survey of materials science: eight routes in six thematic modules spanning bonding and structure, crystallography and XRD, defects and strengthening, phases and transformations, failure and degradation, polymers/ceramics/composites, a synthetic multi-technique lab and a constraints-based selection project. It is original, unreviewed and formative-only.

modifications: Original readings, fictional materials, synthetic datasets, worked examples, practice, retrieval cards and zero-point cases developed with substantial AI assistance on 2026-11-26. All third-party sources are link-only; no source content, code, figure, table, problem or data imported.

knowledge: Atomic structure, chemical bonding, stoichiometry and introductory thermochemistry
Algebra, basic functions and introductory mechanics for property and failure interpretations
prerequisites.statement: General Chemistry I is required. Physics: Mechanics and Calculus I are recommended where the graph permits. Statics & Mechanics of Materials is a linked continuation for derivations intentionally not duplicated here. These project-planned relationships establish no university equivalency.

outcomes.description: Explain how bonding and structure contribute to material classes and functional properties without reducing behavior to a single label.
Use crystallographic notation, cubic spacing and Bragg relationships to interpret bounded synthetic diffraction evidence.
Connect defects, diffusion, slip and strengthening mechanisms with quantitative idealized models and explicit trade-offs.
Interpret binary phase diagrams and transformation models to reason about process–microstructure–property links without operational recipes.
Evaluate mechanical and environmental failure evidence across toughness, creep, fatigue, fracture and corrosion concepts.
Compare polymer molecular distributions and transitions, ceramics, and orientation-dependent composite bounds.
Audit original synthetic multi-technique characterization data while retaining unknowns and non-operational evidence boundaries.
Complete a constraints-first fictional material-selection project with reproducible calculations and unresolved review gates.

lesson_objectives.description: Relate ionic, covalent, metallic and secondary bonding to idealized material structure without treating bond labels as complete property predictions.
Distinguish metals, ceramics, polymers and composites by bonding, structure and processing-sensitive behavior.
Calculate and interpret density, thermal resistance and relative resistivity change for fictional materials while preserving functional-property evidence limits.
Use crystallographic directions, planes and Miller indices with consistent intercept, reduction and sign conventions.
Calculate cubic interplanar spacing and connect plane families to reciprocal geometry.
Apply first-order Bragg reasoning to synthetic XRD records without inferring unmeasured phase, texture or composition.
Classify point, line and interface defects and connect them to diffusion and dislocation-mediated slip.
Compute an Arrhenius diffusion coefficient, steady-state flux and Hall–Petch model value under explicitly idealized assumptions.
Compare solid-solution, grain-size, work and precipitation strengthening while identifying trade-offs and missing evidence.
Read binary phase fields, compositions and phase amounts with tie lines and the lever rule.
Distinguish equilibrium phases from microconstituents and model a synthetic transformation fraction without treating it as universal kinetics.
Connect heat-treatment history to microstructure and properties conceptually without supplying a heat-treatment recipe or fabrication settings.
Differentiate strength, stiffness, ductility and toughness and calculate a synthetic stress–strain energy area.
Link creep, fatigue and fracture evidence using cyclic-damage and stress-intensity models with stated limitations.
Explain galvanic coupling, passivation, pitting and crevice corrosion without assigning real-world compatibility or approval.
Compute Mn, Mw and PDI from a fictional chain population and explain why distribution averages are not interchangeable.
Distinguish Tg, Tm and crystallinity in polymers and relate ceramic bonding and microstructure to typical functional behavior.
Compare composite orientation and Voigt–Reuss bounds while recognizing that bounds are not precise property predictions.
Recompute diffraction spacing, cubic lattice parameter and mass-loss relationships for every synthetic characterization row.
Integrate structural, thermal and mechanical records as separate evidence channels rather than interchangeable identifiers.
Preserve unknown fields, fictional provenance and non-operational limits in a multi-technique interpretation.
Translate fictional service needs into explicit hard constraints and measurable selection criteria before ranking candidates.
Recompute specific stiffness, mass and embodied-energy relationships for all synthetic rehearsal candidates.
Document trade-offs, sensitivity, unknown evidence and non-approval status in a five-milestone material-selection handoff.

modules.title: Bonding, structure, material classes and functional properties

lessons.title: Bonding, structure, material classes and functional properties
lessons.worked_example: For the fictional layer in public practice, R = L/(kA) = 0.020/(200 × 0.005) = 0.020 K/W. A separate fictional specimen has density 54/20 = 2.7 g/cm³. These model values do not identify a real alloy or approve its use.

modules.title: Crystallography, Miller indices, cubic spacing and Bragg XRD

lessons.title: Crystallography, Miller indices, cubic spacing and Bragg XRD
lessons.worked_example: For fictional cubic a = 0.400 nm, d(210) = 0.400/√5 = 0.178885… nm. A separate first-order synthetic reflection with λ = 0.154 nm and d = 0.200 nm has 2θ = 2asin[0.154/(2 × 0.200)] = 45.28748…°.

lessons.title: Defects, diffusion, slip and strengthening
lessons.worked_example: The stipulated Arrhenius inputs give D = 10⁻⁵exp[−80000/(8.314 × 1000)] = 6.62335…×10⁻¹⁰ m²/s. A separate Hall–Petch calculation gives 100 + 0.50/√(4.0×10⁻⁶) = 350 MPa. Both are fictional model outputs, not material qualification.

modules.title: Binary phases, transformations and process–microstructure links

lessons.title: Binary phases, transformations and process–microstructure links
lessons.worked_example: For C₀ = 40, Cα = 20 and CL = 60, liquid fraction = (40−20)/(60−20) = 50%. In a separate fictional kinetic model, X = 1 − exp(−0.020×10²) = 86.4665…%. Equilibrium fractions and transformation kinetics are different claims.

modules.title: Mechanical failure, environmental degradation and fracture links

lessons.title: Mechanical failure, environmental degradation and fracture links
lessons.worked_example: The fictional stress–strain triangle and rectangle contribute 1 and 4 MJ/m³, giving a 5 MJ/m³ toughness proxy. The separate Miner sum is 20,000/100,000 + 300,000/1,000,000 = 0.50; neither number predicts real component life.

modules.title: Polymers, ceramics, composites and integrative applications

lessons.title: Polymers, ceramics, composites and orientation bounds
lessons.worked_example: For the fictional chain population, Mn = 45 kg/mol and Mw = 1000/18 = 55.5555… kg/mol, so PDI = 1.234567…. A separate idealized composite with V₁ = 0.60, E₁ = 200 GPa and E₂ = 20 GPa has Voigt 128 GPa and Reuss 43.478… GPa.

lessons.title: Synthetic multi-technique materials-characterization lab
lessons.worked_example: C02 gives d = 0.154/[2sin(20°)] = 0.225133… nm. C03 mass loss is 3.5%, and C04 gives a = d√3 = 0.356021… nm. Every result is a synthetic record calculation, not an identification or operating procedure.

lessons.title: Constraints-based material-selection project guide
lessons.worked_example: R02 specific stiffness is 120×10⁹/2700 = 44,444,444.444… m²/s². R03 mass is 7800×0.0015 = 11.7 kg, and R04 modeled embodied energy is 2.9×20 = 58 MJ. Hard constraints screen candidates before these trade-offs are compared; no candidate is approved.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt; case checklists are zero-point self-assessments.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous items as content issues.

accessibility.diagram_policy: No copied figures or embedded diagrams are included; crystallographic and process relationships are expressed in prose, equations and tables.
known_issues: Unicode subscripts, superscripts, Greek letters and equations require structured alternatives and assistive-technology review.
CSV tables have not undergone accessibility or usability review.

history.summary: New explicitly partial foundational university survey: eight routes in six modules, eight original substantive readings, 48 public practice items worth 56 points, 24 retrieval cards, two original synthetic CSVs, one zero-point integrative case and five zero-point project milestones. All third-party sources are link-only; no instrument procedure, heat-treatment recipe, fabrication settings, compliance claim or material approval is supplied.

limitations: This eight-route, six-module package is an explicitly partial foundational university survey, not a complete or measured course. It is unreviewed and formative-only; no competency, credit, qualification or institutional authorization is established.

All named materials, scenarios, measurements, properties, microstructures and CSV rows are original synthetic fictional teaching constructions. Arithmetic consistency is not experimental validation, material identification or engineering approval.
Crystallography and characterization work uses supplied records only. No instrument operating procedure, acquisition settings, specimen preparation protocol or laboratory instruction is provided.
Phase-transformation and heat-treatment discussion is conceptual and model-based. No heat-treatment recipe, thermal cycle, fabrication settings or process qualification is provided.
Mechanical and corrosion examples are idealized evidence exercises. They supply no fatigue-life, fracture-life, corrosion-compatibility, fitness-for-service or safety prediction.

Material selection screens fictional rows against declared teaching constraints only. It supplies no standard-specific compliance, certification, procurement decision, design release or material approval.
Statics & Mechanics of Materials retains stress/strain, beam, structural failure and related derivations; this package links that prerequisite/continuation rather than duplicating its derivations.

Of the 24 numerical answers, 0 require units, 0 check significant figures and 0 check dimensions. Every numeric key has an authored absolute tolerance and independent arithmetic/misconception tests; learners must still show units and derivations.
No numeric question uses authored randomization variants in version 0.1.0; all 24 base numeric keys and both public CSV relationships are independently recomputed by the package tests.

Official MIT and reused mechanics, chemistry and biomaterials records are link-only. No third-party prose, figure, table, problem, dataset or asset is imported, and no endorsement or qualified review is implied.
